summary: Forest Service lookout tower on Magazine Mountain, Arkansas's highest point, standing by 1940; no source we read says whether it still stands.

events.note: Forest Service lookout tower stood near the west end of the mountain when a federal survey station was set directly beneath it.

evidence.quote: is the highest point of the U.S. Interior Highlands and the U.S. state of Arkansas
Arkansas - Logan County - St. Francis National Forest

evidence.supports: tower and survey station together on the mountain
evidence.quote: LOOKOUT TOWER AND STATION MAGAZINE WHICH IS DIRECTLY UNDER THE

station described by Coast and Geodetic Survey in 1940

evidence.quote: a partnership with the USDA Forest Service allowed the park to open in 1998 as Mount Magazine State Park

evidence.quote: is within the Ozark-St. Francis National Forests

evidence.supports: park features include hiking trails and a visitor center
evidence.quote: Scenic overlooks, hiking trails, picnic area, pavilion, and visitor center with gift shop add to the amenities.

corrections.why: The state park page says the park is within the Ozark-St. Francis National Forests. The St. Francis name on the Central US Lookouts page appears out of date.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Central US Lookouts page names St. Francis National Forest; the state park page names the Ozark-St. Francis National Forests. The story uses the park page's name.

notes_for_editor: The lookout's build date and its current status are not in any source we read; the 1940 NGS description is the only firm evidence of the tower. The 1959 NGS note mentions a microwave tower at the west end of the mountain but not the lookout, which may matter for the fate of the tower; a human should check. The 1938 and 1941 forest dates and the 1998 park date come from Wikipedia, which cites its own sources; check against Forest Service records if the story is published. Record's name 'Magazine Mountain' is fine.
